Affinity vector

Generated by TestReport in pkg/distillery/stills/affinity. The personalization vector is what the affinity still distills from a shopper's choices — selections, views and carts — and what the shop ranks every listing with. This report shows how Fade.Vector lets it follow a shopper whose intent changes: how fast the past fades, when the change detection steps in, and what the vector reads as along the way. The histories are the shape TestIntentPicksUpQuickly checks: a visit every two days, the persona changing every six visits.

The fade

Every choice fades everything before it by the same factor, so recency is counted in choices, not in time: a shopper who comes back after three weeks is not a stranger. The still holds only the newest {{.Keep}} choices, drawing off the rest, far beyond what the mock data reach. A visit has about ten choices.

On top of the fade, a change of intent forgets faster. After every choice the last {{.Fade.Recent}} contributions are compared with the rest of the vector, over the dimensions both name. When their cosine falls below {{.Fade.Shift}}, the shopper is taken to want something else now and the rest collapses to {{.Fade.Collapse}} of itself. A step into a new category's own dimensions — clothes to cushions — shares too little to compare and never triggers it.

Strong changes

Kate, then Sofia, then Lena, then Mira: {{.StrongChoices}} choices, {{.StrongCollapse}} collapses. The first two changes are strong — the tastes do not overlap — so the cosine should drop below the threshold within the first choices of the new intent, collapse the past, and let the new persona take over the vector straight after. The third, Lena to Mira, is gentle: both are minimal and modern, the detection stays quiet and the fade carries the vector across — as in the next section. Hover a chart for every value.

A gentle change

Mira, then Lena: tastes that overlap — both minimal and modern. Lena's picks do not point away from what the vector holds, so the change detection should not fire ({{.GentleCollapse}} collapses); the fade alone carries the vector across, more slowly.

Changing intent

What TestIntentPicksUpQuickly checks, visit by visit: long histories through the shop as it is, a visit every two days, the persona — the intent — changing every six visits, every direction of change between the personas. Each visit shows who was shopping and three checks: L the landing page, ranked before the visit, opens on something the intent likes; C so does the visit's closing look; V the vector the still distills after the visit reads as that persona. A strong change, to a taste that does not overlap the old one, should be read on its first visit and served by its second; a gentle one, between overlapping tastes, within a few. The vector fades per event and collapses its past when the recent picks point clearly elsewhere.

Against a flat sum and a decay by time

The same history read three ways after every visit: summed flat, decayed by time (a one-week half-life), and faded per choice. The flat sum never lets go of the first intent; time decay follows, but only as fast as the calendar allows; the fade follows the choices.
